summary: Poisson GLM (log link) for French motor TPL claim frequency (GLM1 of Noll, Salzmann & Wuthrich 2018). Raw freMTPL2freq is read with quote="\"'" (single quotes stripped from strings), ClaimNb capped at 4 and Exposure at 1, then GLM features are engineered: AreaGLM (A..F -> 1..6, continuous), VehPowerGLM (factor, capped at 9), VehAgeGLM (3 classes, ref '2'), DrivAgeGLM (7 age bands, ref '5'), BonusMalusGLM (capped at 150), DensityGLM (log Density), VehBrand (ref B1), Region (ref R24), VehGas (factor). A seeded 90/10 random split (set.seed(100); sample) produces learn/test. glm(ClaimNb ~ ..., offset = log(Exposure), family = poisson()) is fitted on learn; fitted() on learn and predict(type='response') on test, both including the log(Exposure) offset.

preprocessing.description: Read raw CSV; both double and single quotes act as quote characters, so string values such as 'A' become A. Column names are already syntactic (make.names is a no-op). No rows dropped.
Integer code of Area factor (levels sorted A..F -> 1..6); used as a continuous covariate.
Cap VehPower at 9 and treat as factor with levels 4..9 (numeric order), reference '4'.

preprocessing.r_code:
VehAgeGLM <- cbind(c(0:110), c(1, rep(2, 10), rep(3, 100)))
dat$VehAgeGLM <- as.factor(VehAgeGLM[dat$VehAge + 1, 2])
dat[, "VehAgeGLM"] <- relevel(dat[, "VehAgeGLM"], ref = "2")
preprocessing.description: Lookup table: VehAge 0 -> 1, 1..10 -> 2, 11..110 -> 3 (VehAge > 110 would give NA). Factor releveled so '2' is the reference; level order 2,1,3. The matrix column index 2 is the class column of the local lookup matrix, not a data column.

preprocessing.r_code:
DrivAgeGLM <- cbind(c(18:100), c(rep(1, 21 - 18), rep(2, 26 - 21), rep(3, 31 - 26), rep(4, 41 - 31), rep(5, 51 - 41), rep(6, 71 - 51), rep(7, 101 - 71)))
dat$DrivAgeGLM <- as.factor(DrivAgeGLM[dat$DrivAge - 17, 2])
dat[, "DrivAgeGLM"] <- relevel(dat[, "DrivAgeGLM"], ref = "5")
preprocessing.description: Lookup table: DrivAge 18-20 -> 1, 21-25 -> 2, 26-30 -> 3, 31-40 -> 4, 41-50 -> 5, 51-70 -> 6, 71-100 -> 7 (DrivAge > 100 would give NA). Releveled so '5' is reference; level order 5,1,2,3,4,6,7.
VehBrand factor with reference B1 (levels in captured xlevels order).

preprocessing.r_code:
set.seed(100)
ll <- sample(c(1:nrow(dat)), round(0.9 * nrow(dat)), replace = FALSE)
learn <- dat[ll, ]
test <- dat[-ll, ]
preprocessing.description: Random 90/10 split. Not re-implemented: membership is supplied by the harness from the frozen R split (split.csv).

model.formula: ClaimNb ~ VehPowerGLM + VehAgeGLM + DrivAgeGLM + BonusMalusGLM + VehBrand + VehGas + DensityGLM + Region + AreaGLM, offset = log(Exposure)

randomness: set.seed(100); sample(1:nrow(dat), round(0.9*nrow(dat))) selects the learn rows; test is the complement. The split is not re-implemented in Python (R-RNG-01); the harness supplies train/test membership from output/m1_fremtpl2/model/reference/split.csv.
risks: GOV-01: DrivAge (age, a protected characteristic) enters the model as the 7-band factor DrivAgeGLM; migrated faithfully, requires actuarial justification under UK Equality Act 2010 Sch.3 para 20A, to be assessed by validation.
Data capping (ClaimNb <= 4, Exposure <= 1) treats outliers as data errors without row-level justification; reproduced as written.

Lookup tables for VehAge (0..110) and DrivAge (18..100) silently yield NA for out-of-range values (DrivAge < 18 would mis-index or error in R); current data appears within range, but future data outside the range would produce NA predictions. Python reproduces NA for values above the table range.
AreaGLM uses the factor integer code of Area as a continuous variable, imposing a linear ordinal effect A..F.
Region and VehBrand references (R24, B1) are hard-coded; a new level in future data would yield an unmappable dummy (NA prediction in Python).
The learn/test split depends on R's RNG (set.seed(100), sample); it is not reproducible in Python and is taken from the frozen R capture.
String values in the source file are wrapped in single quotes; parity depends on stripping them exactly as read.csv(quote="\"'") does (R-IO-04).
